boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Goldsboro Expedition. Preserve per-engagement dates: Kinston December 14, White Hall December 16 and Goldsborough Bridge December 17, 1862. Skirmishes on other days (Southwest Creek, Mount Olive, Thompson's Bridge) are not added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Foster's 1st Division and Evans's Brigade without counts; the live field reads zero. Foster reports leaving New Berne with about 10,000 infantry, 40 guns and about 640 cavalry, and put the Kinston enemy at about 6,000 with twenty guns. Smith reports Evans had 2,000 men, and on December 15 relayed an estimate of 30,000 for Foster.
claims.rationale: Each commander's estimate of the other differs sharply from the other's own figure; none is adopted. Foster's total is the whole expedition at departure, not Kinston's engaged force.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Foster reports taking Kinston, eleven guns and 400 or 500 prisoners; Smith says Evans withdrew with small loss to the left bank of the Neuse.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Captures are Foster's claims, not inspected inventories.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 685 total; the live NPS field reads 685 total (US 160; CS 525;). Foster's December 14 report estimated his loss at not over 200 killed and wounded; Smith says most of about 400 Confederate missing were taken at Kinston Bridge.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Foster's figure is an early estimate; Smith's missing figure is expedition-wide.

open_questions: Returns, the compiler's revised Union casualty statement (p.60, not inspected), Evans's own report and the Kinston command clock remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Foster's reports and G. W. Smith's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XVIII, are two further families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
